newsitem.title: USA: Opening arguments to begin in Simpson civil trial.
newsitem.headline: Opening arguments to begin in Simpson civil trial.

text.p: More than a year after O.J. Simpson was acquitted of murder, opening statements were set to begin on Wednesday in the former football star's civil trial with his attorneys again expected to argue that he was framed.

But unlike his criminal trial, Simpson will have to take the witness stand and explain exactly what he was doing the night his ex-wife Nicole Brown Simpson and her friend Ronald Goldman were slashed to death.

"A lot will hinge on Mr. Simpson's testimony, especially if it is early in the trial. The jury will pay a lot of attention to what he says," said Richard Rosenthal, the lawyer for Faye Resnick, a friend of Nicole Simpson.
Rosenthal said he believed the jury in the civil trial might be more inclined to find Simpson responsible for the murders.

But some legal analysts have cautioned against drawing any snap judgments about the jurors, some of whom seemed receptive during jury selection to defence arguments that police planted or contaminated evidence to implicate Simpson.
Simpson, who never took the stand at the criminal trial, was acquitted of the murders on Oct. 3, 1995, by a mostly black jury.

Now his fate will be decided by a mostly white jury in the more affluent seaside town of Santa Monica. If Simpson is found responsible for the deaths, he could be forced to pay millions of dollars in damages.

Resnick, who wrote a book about her friendship with Nicole Simpson and talked about Simpson's alleged abuse of his ex-wife, has not been subpoenaed to testify at the civil trial, but the defence has made it clear it wants to question another key player in the case, ex-detective Mark Fuhrman.
Simpson's lead attorney told prospective jurors last week that he intended to confront police officers on the witness stand to prove his theory that evidence was planted.
Robert Baker made it clear the thrust of the defence would be that one or more officers planted evidence to incriminate him and that other evidence was tampered with or deliberately contaminated.

He said he would be asking officers and FBI experts tough and confrontational questions to prove his point, and asked the prospective panellists if they would be comfortable with that. Most said they would.

Fuhrman, one of the first detectives at the murder scene, and the man who discovered some of the key evidence, pleaded no contest to a charge of perjury earlier this month and was sentenced to three years' probation.

Baker said on Monday that Fuhrman "will be a witness in this case regardless of whether he is present or not present," so the defence should be allowed to refer to his perjury plea and his alleged racist views during the civil trial.
Lawyers for the families of the murder victims want to bar the defence from referring to Fuhrman's no-contest plea to perjury and from talking about his alleged racism.
Judge Hiroshi Fujisaki will rule on the motion first thing on Wednesday.

Resnick's lawyer Rosenthal said of possible Fuhrman testimony: "I have a problem with whether it is relevant to whether O.J. Simpson is liable for the deaths. His lack of credibility makes Fuhrman not a very useful witness."
On the defence tactics of proving Simpson was framed, the lawyer did not see it being successful.
"It seems for the jury to buy it, the defence must prove such a conspiracy existed and I don't see any evidence."
Fujisaki has barred TV cameras from the trial.
